title: Detecting Architecture Erosion
objectives: Audit import graphs for layering violations
Use coupling signals from code review
Keep boundaries honest with checklists and tooling

examples.name: audit.txt
examples.code:
# signals to hunt
- deep imports into feature internals (bypassing index.ts)
- shared/ importing features
- components importing api clients directly
- one store imported by 90% of files (god store)

# tooling ideas
- dependency-cruiser / eslint boundaries to codify the graph
- PR checklist: "which arrows did this PR add?"

exercise.prompt: Classify each finding: "shared imports feature" (layering violation), "feature uses its own index" (healthy), "component calls fetch directly" (boundary bypass), "two features import each other" (cycle).
hints: Any upward import from shared/ is a violation.
Direct fetch in components bypasses the service layer.

options: the PR review question "which dependency arrows did this add?"
questions.explanation: Review-time attention to dependency direction stops erosion before it lands.

options: unowned state that will resist every change
questions.explanation: When everything depends on one module, nothing can change in isolation.
